text:
Sam Turner: quick thread — after today's profiling the kernel routing tweak increased p99 token latency for long-prefix workloads by ~7%. I put together a lightweight metrics schema proposal to track kernel selection, batching behavior, and KV impact without exploding label cardinality.

Nina Park: can you paste the raw perf numbers and current labels?

Sam Turner: perf summary: p50 26ms -> 25ms, p95 62ms -> 63ms, p99 210ms -> 225ms (long prefixes >1024). Regression spikes correlate with batch sizes that hit fallback kernels.

Junaid Ali: important to separate queuing vs compute vs kv lookup. Do we have token-level stage metrics today?

Sam Turner: we have token_latency_seconds but it's a single histogram. proposal splits into stage histograms to make root-cause easier: token_latency.{queue,kv,compute,decode}_seconds. keeps metric cardinality low but gives stage breakdown.

Kevin Zhou: agree. also recommend NOT putting request_id, exact model_revision, or prompt_hash as labels. that destroyed cardinality in past.

Sam Turner: yes — naming sketch (prom-like):

```
metric: inference_token_latency_seconds
labels:
  route: <route_name>                 # e.g. checkout-search (coarse)
  model_family: <family>             # llama2, mixtral, etc. (coarse)
  model_size: <size_bucket>          # small|base|large (coarse)
  kernel_name: <kernel>              # fused|matmul|sparse (low-card)
  kernel_release: <semver>           # to version kernels
  kernel_variant: <variant_bucket>   # e.g. fastpath|fallback (very small set)
  batch_bucket: '<1|1-8|8-32|32+'    # pre-bucketed to control cardinality
  kv_hit: 'yes|no'
  schema_v: 'v2'                     # metric schema version
```

Nina Park: bucketed batch sizes are 👍. Are we okay with kernel_release as a label? versions can proliferate.

Sam Turner: good point. keep kernel_release but limit to major.minor (e.g. 1.4). we'll rotate old releases out and provide rollup rules in the backend.

Olivia Perez: how do we track prefix-length effects? we need to know when KV cache prevents compute vs when long prefix forces different kernel.

Sam Turner: avoid raw prefix_len as label. instead expose prefix_bucket same style: '<0|1-64|65-512|513-1024|1025+'. Also add kv_prefix_match: 'full|partial|none' computed by runtime (low-card).

Junaid Ali: dashboard ideas: per-route KPI card with p50/p95/p99 for token compute and kv latency stacked, plus a heatmap of kernel_variant x batch_bucket showing error bars.

Kevin Zhou: +1. also per-model_family/route uptime of fastpath kernel (ratio of kernel_variant==fastpath over total) — useful for canary alerts.

Sam Turner: alerting suggestions: alert when p99 compute latency increases 3x over baseline for a route AND fastpath_ratio drops >20%. Avoid alerts for individual kernel_release churn.

Nina Park: migration plan? we'll need schema_v to allow multiple versions. Backend should map old labels to new ones and keep rollups.

Sam Turner: migration steps I propose:
1) instrument token stage histograms and the new low-card labels behind a flag.
2) collect both old and new for 2 weeks.
3) enable dashboards that use schema_v='v2' and iterate.
4) remove legacy expensive labels after validation.

Olivia Perez: can we also emit a sparse event log for individual regression traces (sampled 1/1000) with full metadata to S3/trace store? metrics stay low-card, traces carry high-card debug info.

Sam Turner: exactly — metrics for aggregation, sampled traces for debugging.

metrics-bot: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/metrics/pulls/238 — includes config, dashboard JSON, and migration playbook. :tada:

Kevin Zhou: I'll review the PR. quick comment: prefer snake_case for labels (kernel_name, kernel_release) and dot-separated metric names (inference.token_latency_seconds) so we are consistent with infra style.

Sam Turner: fine with snake_case for labels. I used prom-like keys for readability. We'll standardize in the PR.

Junaid Ali: one more thing — add a fallback metric: token_latency_fallback_ratio by route/model_family to quickly quantify how often we hit fallback kernels.

Sam Turner: added to PR.

Nina Park: thanks. i'll prototype the dashboard widgets for route-level KPIs and heatmaps this week.

Olivia Perez: will set up sample trace schema for S3 and add the ingest hook in runtime.

Sam Turner: cool — let's keep the schema tight and iterate. if folks can review PR + dashboard mock by EOD Friday that'd be great.

Kevin Zhou: noted, review incoming.

Sam Turner: thanks all.
